title: Transactions & ACID
html:
A transaction groups several statements into one unit of work that either fully happens or not at all. It is what makes a money transfer safe.

ACID

PropertyGuaranteeMechanism
AtomicityAll statements succeed, or none take effectUndo/rollback log
ConsistencyEach transaction moves the DB from one valid state to another (constraints hold)Constraints, triggers, your logic
IsolationConcurrent transactions don't see each other's partial work (to a chosen degree)Locks and/or MVCC snapshots
DurabilityOnce committed, changes survive crashes and power lossWrite-ahead log (WAL) flushed to disk

BEGIN, COMMIT, ROLLBACK

When a statement fails

A transfer of 1500 breaks the CHECK (balance >= 0) constraint on the debit:

Watch out

In most engines, only the failing statement is undone automatically — the earlier credit is still pending inside the open transaction. The application must catch the error and issue ROLLBACK (PostgreSQL goes further: the whole transaction is marked aborted and only ROLLBACK is accepted). Drivers and ORMs usually wrap this in a with transaction: block.

Savepoints: partial rollback

Autocommit

Outside an explicit BEGIN, most engines run in autocommit mode: every statement is its own transaction. Oracle is the exception — a transaction starts implicitly and you must COMMIT. Python's DB-API and many drivers open transactions for you and require conn.commit().

Do

Keep transactions short: do the reads and computation first, then BEGIN → writes → COMMIT. Long transactions hold locks, block other users and bloat MVCC history.

Explain ACID with a bank transfer.

Atomicity: debit and credit both apply or neither does. Consistency: balances never go negative and total money is preserved (constraints). Isolation: a concurrent report never sees money “in flight” (debited but not yet credited). Durability: once the user sees “transfer complete”, a crash can't undo it.

What is the difference between COMMIT and ROLLBACK?

COMMIT makes all changes of the transaction permanent and visible to others. ROLLBACK discards them, restoring the state at BEGIN (or at a SAVEPOINT with ROLLBACK TO).
